findings.reason: Untrusted source: batadv_recv_unicast_packet() is the rx handler for batman-adv unicast frames registered in batadv_rx_handler[] and dispatched from batadv_batman_skb_recv() (net/batman-adv/main.c:484), i.e. a ptype receive handler fed by eth_type_trans output; an attacker on the L2 segment can send ETH_P_BATMAN frames. Missing guarantee: on entry the only linear-area guarantee is batadv_batman_skb_recv()'s pskb_may_pull(skb, 2) (net/batman-adv/main.c:452), so with a non-linear skb (frags/frag_list from GRO or SG receive) only 2 bytes are guaranteed in the head, yet this function casts skb->data to struct batadv_unicast_packet and immediately reads unicast_packet->packet_type (offset 0, 1 byte, so this specific read is inside the 2-byte guarantee). The violated invariant is the pattern, but the single packet_type byte at offset 0 is actually within the 2 pulled bytes; however hdr_size is then chosen as sizeof(struct batadv_unicast_4addr_packet) (20 bytes) and later batadv_check_unicast_packet()/batadv_check_unicast_ttvn() pull only hdr_len+ETH_HLEN before unicast_4addr_packet->subtype/src are read at lines 993-1000 - those reads ARE guarded. The unguarded read is therefore only the 1-byte packet_type at offset 0, which the 2-byte entry pull covers, so the out-of-bounds read is NOT reachable via this line alone. Counterevidence checked: (a) batadv_batman_skb_recv pskb_may_pull(skb,2) at main.c:452 guarantees offsets 0-1 linear; (b) packet_type is byte 0; (c) version byte 1 is checked in main.c:473; (d) all later struct reads (lines 971, 994, 1020 area) are preceded by batadv_check_unicast_packet pskb_may_pull(hdr_size) (routing.c:447) and batadv_check_unicast_ttvn pskb_may_pull(hdr_len+ETH_HLEN) (routing.c:798) plus skb_cow; (e) batadv_recv_my_icmp_packet/batadv_recv_icmp_ttl_exceeded similarly read only after batadv_recv_icmp_packet's pskb_may_pull(hdr_size) (routing.c:350). Mechanism if the entry pull were absent would be a slab OOB read past the linear head of a non-linear received skb; as written, the observable defect is the pre-pull dereference pattern (pointer into linear area used before presence guaranteed), which is exactly the branch invariant even though the concrete byte is within the 2-byte guarantee.
findings.conclusion: batadv_recv_unicast_packet dereferences skb->data as a struct header before any pull in this function; only the 2-byte entry pull covers byte 0, so the pattern matches the branch but the concrete OOB is bounded - report as medium-confidence hypothesis.

findings.reason: Untrusted source: batadv_route_unicast_packet() is reached from batadv_recv_unicast_packet()/batadv_recv_unhandled_unicast_packet() (routing.c:928, 1028) for any received unicast batman frame. Checks before use: its callers did pskb_may_pull(hdr_size) via batadv_check_unicast_packet (hdr_size >= sizeof(struct batadv_unicast_packet) = 10) and pskb_may_pull(hdr_len + ETH_HLEN) in batadv_check_unicast_ttvn (routing.c:798), so unicast_packet->ttl (offset 2) and ->dest (offset 4, ETH_ALEN bytes) reads are within pulled linear bytes for the normal UNICAST path. However, batadv_recv_unhandled_unicast_packet sets hdr_size = sizeof(struct batadv_unicast_packet) too, so both paths pull at least 10 bytes before routing. Counterevidence: skb_cow in check_unicast_ttvn re-cows but does not shrink headlen; no read in this function exceeds the 10-byte header that callers guarantee. ethhdr = eth_hdr(skb) at line 659 reads the mac header which eth_type_trans keeps linear by construction. So the ttl/dest reads are guarded by caller pulls; remaining concern is only the pattern of re-deriving the pointer after skb_cow (which the code does correctly at line 685-686).
findings.conclusion: batadv_route_unicast_packet reads ttl/dest after callers pulled >=10 bytes, so the reads are guarded; only the pattern (pre-pull struct deref) matches the branch - low actionable value, kept for the record as medium-confidence variant of the same pattern.

candidates.reason: unicast_packet->packet_type read from skb->data before any pull in batadv_recv_unicast_packet; entry guarantees only 2 linear bytes (net/batman-adv/main.c:452 pskb_may_pull(skb,2)); packet_type is byte 0 so it is within that guarantee, and later 4addr reads are guarded by batadv_check_unicast_packet/check_unicast_ttvn pulls (routing.c:447, 798)
candidates.conclusion: Pattern finding: struct cast of skb->data plus deref before this function's own pskb_may_pull; concrete byte is covered by the caller's 2-byte pull, so impact is bounded - verify whether any batadv rx handler reads past byte 1 before its own pull.

OGM2 walk bounded by batadv_check_management_packet(BATADV_OGM2_HLEN) pull (bat_v_ogm.c:1000) and batadv_v_ogm_aggr_packet comparing next_buff_pos to skb_headlen(skb) (bat_v_ogm.c:829-844), so only linear bytes are parsed

coverage_gaps: drivers/net/ was only pattern-sampled (CAN/arcnet/ethernet driver casts of skb->data are TX-path or driver-local linear buffers); the ~2900-file tree was not exhaustively audited for receive parsers lacking pulls.
Protocols building skbs in driver-owned linear memory (CAN, arcnet, ATM lane) were assumed linear by construction; no per-driver verification of skb_headlen was done.
mac80211/wpa/tkip/wep and lib80211 skb->data header casts were not individually audited; mac80211 rx paths mostly linearize via ieee80211_data_to_8023 but this was not verified line-by-line.
limitations: No build, KASAN run, or reproducer was possible (read-only snapshot, no network); all conclusions rest on static reading of the exact supplied lines.

The primary finding (batadv_recv_unicast_packet) is a pattern match where the concrete dereferenced byte (packet_type at offset 0) lies within the 2-byte pskb_may_pull performed by the entry dispatcher, so an actual out-of-bounds read was not established; it is reported as a medium-confidence hypothesis per the branch definition.

Whether received batman-adv skbs can actually be non-linear at batadv_batman_skb_recv depends on the underlying hard-interface driver's SG/GRO configuration, which is deployment-dependent and unverified.
Snapshot revision is opaque; line numbers are valid only for snapshots/s01 as supplied.
